rubrics.rubric: Does the Audit sheet accurately reconcile the protocol with the trial data and explain the power implications of material discrepancies?
criterion: The Audit sheet uses the required columns Parameter, Protocol Value, Observed Value, and Discrepancy Flag.
The audit compares protocol and observed enrollment and allocation.
The audit compares the protocol design and primary-analysis specification with the available trial data.
The audit compares the assumed common standard deviation with an observed pooled standard deviation calculated from the primary endpoint.
The audit compares assumed and observed dropout or Week 24 missingness.
Each material discrepancy includes a source-grounded implication for the study's actual precision or power.

rubrics.rubric: Does the Site Effects analysis correctly implement the protocol-specified ITT-LOCF endpoint, identify the outlier site, and perform the leave-one-site-out sensitivity analysis?
criterion: Every randomized subject is included in the ITT endpoint after applying LOCF as specified in the protocol.
The number of imputed subjects and the value carried forward for each observed missingness pattern are documented.
Per-site Drug_X minus Placebo treatment effects report the sample size in each arm.
Per-site Drug_X minus Placebo treatment effects report an estimate and 95% confidence interval.
The outlier designation follows a stated sign-consistent rule for the largest treatment benefit under the required per-site analysis.
The leave-one-site-out table excludes every site once.
Each leave-one-site-out result reports the protocol-adjusted overall treatment difference, 95% confidence interval, and p-value.
The interpretation states whether the overall conclusion is sensitive to excluding the outlier or any other site.

rubrics.rubric: Does the Subgroup Forest sheet report the required mixed-effects model, subgroup effects, interaction tests, and clinically meaningful interpretation?
criterion: The mixed-effects model treats site as a random effect and includes baseline HbA1c.
The mixed-effects model includes treatment, age group, sex, treatment-by-age-group, and treatment-by-sex fixed effects, or a mathematically equivalent hierarchical parameterization.
A coefficient table reports estimates and inferential results for the fitted model.
Treatment effects with 95% confidence intervals are reported for age under 65, age 65 or older, Male, Female, and Overall.

The forest plot displays the five required effects with 95% confidence intervals and a vertical reference line at zero; the adjacent estimate-and-CI table is accepted as corroborating evidence for the plotted values of an embedded workbook chart.

The treatment-by-age-group and treatment-by-sex p-values are annotated on or immediately adjacent to the forest plot; an adjacent table is accepted as evidence of those annotations for an embedded workbook chart.
The interpretation separately addresses statistical significance at p < 0.05 and clinical relevance of the observed subgroup differences.
The interpretation relates subgroup consistency or heterogeneity to regulatory expectations without claiming equivalence from a non-significant test.

rubrics.rubric: Does the Sample Size sheet correctly re-estimate the 52-week extension sample size for both required scenarios?
criterion: The two scenarios use the full-dataset effect and the effect after excluding the identified outlier site.
Each scenario uses 80% of its observed treatment effect as the target difference.
Each scenario uses an observed pooled standard deviation and documents the population used to estimate it.
The calculation uses 90% power and two-sided alpha 0.05.
The calculation follows the cited two-sample parallel-group means formula or a mathematically equivalent method.
Each scenario reports per-arm and total sample sizes before dropout adjustment.
Each scenario reports per-arm and total sample sizes after a 15% dropout adjustment.
Rounding and any uncertainty or modeling assumptions are stated.

rubrics.rubric: Does the Sample Size sheet compute conditional power for Week 24 from the observed Week 12 interim data?
criterion: Conditional power is framed as the probability of significance at Week 24 given the Week 12 interim result.
The calculation uses the observed Week 12 treatment effect or its corresponding test statistic.
The calculation uses the protocol-planned final sample size.
The interim information fraction is shown and its derivation is stated.
A valid interim-to-final conditional-power formula is shown.
The observed interim Z-statistic and two-sided critical value are shown.
The reported conditional power is numerically consistent with the displayed inputs, allowing ordinary rounding.

rubrics.rubric: Does the RWE Comparison sheet perform the requested source-grounded A1C-testing and medication-utilization comparisons?
criterion: A1C testing is defined as an A1Cresult value that is neither missing nor "None".
A1C testing is reported by every admission type represented in diabetic_data.csv using labels decoded from IDS_mapping.csv.
Each admission-type row reports the tested numerator, encounter denominator, and proportion.
An overall A1C testing numerator, denominator, and proportion are reported.
Real-world metformin and insulin use are calculated using the instruction's any-value-other-than-"No" rule.
Trial baseline metformin and insulin history are reported separately by treatment arm.
The medication table contrasts the real-world rate with the trial-arm rates for metformin and insulin.

The GLP-1 comparison assesses field availability in both the real-world and trial baseline sources, distinguishes unavailable or unsuitable data from an observed zero, and states the resulting limitation.
Trial medication rates use the corresponding baseline history fields and treatment-arm denominators.

rubrics.rubric: Does the submission provide the complete, internally consistent deliverable requested by the instructions?
criterion: The output includes DX24_301_Integrity_Analysis.xlsx.
The workbook contains sheets named exactly Audit, Site Effects, Subgroup Forest, Sample Size, and RWE Comparison.

A forest plot is embedded in the workbook or supplied as a separate image deliverable; a separate image is not required when an embedded chart has its complete underlying estimate, confidence-interval, and interaction-p-value table on the sheet.
Treatment-effect signs, outlier identity, imputation counts, and scenario labels are consistent across sheets.
Displayed totals and headline results are traceable to formulas, tables, or documented calculations using the named inputs.
